clue.text: Not much to drink (much less than a full finger in fact)

definitions.text: Not much to drink (much less than a full finger in fact)

parts.words: Not much to drink (much less than a full finger in fact)
parts.note: a tiny measure of drink, pictured as the amount held by the little cap a seamstress wears on a fingertip, far less than a finger of whisky

explanation.surface: A drinker is served a stingy measure, well short of a full finger of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'finger' of whisky is a bar measure, but here the finger is literal: the drink fits inside the sewing cap worn on one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny quantity of liquid, the amount a sewing fingertip cover could hold, is a common idiom for a very small drink.

clue.text: Wine from well-respected source spiked by narcotic drug (not aural)

indicators.note: a drink that has been spiked is tampered with, so the letters are interfered with and rearranged
not tells us to take away the letters for the word that follows from the word before

parts.note: otic is a technical word meaning relating to the ear, the same as aural

explanation.surface: A fine wine from a reputable supplier turns out to have been laced with drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not aural)' removes OTIC from NARCOTIC, leaving NARC; with DRUG that gives NARCDRUG, which 'spiked' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand cru is a top-ranked vineyard, especially in Burgundy and Bordeaux, and by extension its wine.

clue.text: Perhaps Mozart's class stifling Salieri ultimately

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a genus is a class or kind in biological classification

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word it qualifies

explanation.surface: Salieri was smothered by the brilliance of Mozart's class, as legend tells of the rival composers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the definition as 'Mozart's ___', what Mozart had, perhaps; the I at the end of Salieri goes inside GENUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart is the classic example of exceptional natural talent, so his gift is the standard instance of brilliance.

clue.text: Unimportant employee guarding Latin block

indicators.note: a guard surrounds what it protects, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: a cog in the machine is a minor worker in a big organisation

explanation.surface: A lowly worker stands watch over a block of Latin text.
explanation.definitionFit: To clog a pipe or drain is to block it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: One possibly viewing a crime as a mark of King Edward, joker and crime-fighter?

parts.note: King Edward is a British potato variety, and an eye is a mark on a potato's skin
a wit is a joker or comedian
Eliot Ness was the American lawman who pursued Al Capone

explanation.surface: A list of colourful characters, a monarch, a comic and a lawman, as possible observers of a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward reads as the monarch, but it is the British potato variety, whose skin marks are eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sees a crime happen and can testify about it is the person meant.

clue.text: As the procrastinator says in honour of easy listening music scene?

parts.note: a toast is drunk 'to' someone, in their honour
MOR stands for middle of the road, bland easy-listening music
making a scene means causing a row, a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A pun about raising a glass to the soft-music crowd, put in the mouth of someone who always delays.
explanation.definitionFit: A procrastinator always puts things off, promising to do them on the next day.

clue.text: Switches pins

definitions.meaning: switches are thin flexible canes or rods
pins is slang for legs, which are also called by this name in slang

explanation.definitionFit: Thin canes are rods of wood, and in old slang legs are also called by the same word.

clue.text: Scary word applied to top of tree trunk

parts.note: boo is the word shouted to startle someone

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the word in a down clue

explanation.surface: A ghost story about a frightening shout attached to the top of a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Trunk looks like part of the tree, but it is the American word for a car's luggage space.
explanation.definitionFit: The luggage compartment of a car is called a trunk in American English.

clue.text: "Equus" mundanely lacks the space for tomfoolery

parts.note: Peter Shaffer's Equus, described in plain words, is a stage drama about a horse, so it is a horse play
Peter Shaffer's Equus, described in plain words, is a stage drama about a horse, so it is a horse play

explanation.surface: Equus, put plainly, without its gap between words, becomes boisterous fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks the space' says the two words describing Equus run together into one.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough boisterous fooling around is a synonym for tomfoolery.

clue.text: Possibly caught in the field with social cap

parts.note: in cricket a batter caught by a fielder is out, one of several ways to be dismissed
a do is a party or social gathering

explanation.surface: A fielder takes a catch, then everyone heads off to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Cap looks like a hat, but here it is the verb meaning to top or better something.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap a story or joke is to better it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Cold in skimpy garment — no good being a sausage maker?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a mini is a very short skirt
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone shivers in a tiny skirt, no use for anything, not even working in a butcher's.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: grinding meat is what a sausage maker does.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage maker grinds meat into small pieces, so the participle describes the work being done.

clue.text: Artist's impression of trees spurned

parts.note: a wood is a group of trees
to cut someone is to snub or spurn them

explanation.surface: An artist sketches a grove of trees that has been rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: A print made from a carved block of timber is an impression an artist takes from it.

clue.text: A tail-less, devouring creature's place

indicators.note: tail-less means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a locust is the insect that devours crops in swarms

explanation.surface: A tailless beast eating everything in its path has its own spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Locus is Latin for place, used in English for a site or position, as in a locus of power.

clue.text: It's moored at sea, like a power boat

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boat tied up in harbour is described as engine-driven.
explanation.definitionFit: A power boat is driven by an engine rather than sails or oars, so it is engine-powered.

clue.text: The state of Hattie Jacques in more than one film

definitions.text: The state of Hattie Jacques in more than one film

parts.words: The state of Hattie Jacques in more than one film
parts.note: Hattie Jacques played the senior hospital nurse in several of Britain's Carry On comedy films, so the condition of being that character

explanation.surface: A question about the condition of a British comic actress across a series of films.
explanation.walkthrough: Hattie Jacques was a British comedy actress, famous as the hospital's formidable senior nurse in the Carry On films.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -hood names a condition, so being the senior nurse is the state of holding that post.

clue.text: Rob's insult about unprofessional law enforcement teams

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: diss is slang for insult or disrespect
posses are groups of citizens rounded up by a sheriff to help catch outlaws

explanation.surface: Rob insults the amateur bands of lawmen who come after him.
explanation.definitionFit: To rob someone of property is to take it away from them, a synonym.

clue.text: Guardian's line in Truss discussion such as 4,8,22 and 23 down

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: to truss is to bind, as is to fetter
the setter writes for the Guardian, which calls itself ours
words are a discussion, as in having words

explanation.surface: The Guardian's position on Lynne Truss's discussion of swearing, illustrated by four answers.
explanation.walkthrough: Lynne Truss wrote a book about rudeness, but she is a red herring: here 'Truss' is the verb meaning bind, and 'Guardian's' is the newspaper speaking of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: CLOG, BOOT, PUMP and MULE all have four letters, a literal fit beside the swearing sense.

clue.text: Team sport, unlike this clue, accommodated by the French

indicators.note: to be accommodated by something is to be housed within it

parts.note: le is French for the
this clue runs down, so the opposite is across

explanation.surface: A team game, quite unlike this puzzle clue, is taken in by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a field game played by teams using netted sticks.

clue.text: Swede's description of tripe including round cut

indicators.note: including means holding something inside

parts.note: tripe is slang for nonsense, as is rot
O is round in shape
to crop is to cut short

explanation.surface: A Swedish person describes tripe with a round slice taken out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swede looks like a person from Sweden, but it is the vegetable, called rutabaga in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: A swede is a vegetable grown for its edible underground part, so this is its category.

clue.text: Silly game interrupted by independent credit setters

indicators.note: something interrupted has another piece break into it

parts.note: ludo is a board game played with dice and counters
CR is the abbreviation for credit in accounts
crossword setters refer to themselves as we or us

explanation.surface: A foolish game is held up by independent setters taking credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridiculous and absurd things are silly, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Gentleman Bottom raised the remains of a wreck

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: sir is a title or form of address for a gentleman
a bed is the bottom of the sea or a river

explanation.surface: A gentleman lifts his posterior from the scattered wreckage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SIRBED round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattered fragments left after something is wrecked are this kind of rubble.

clue.text: Glad you said that's "overdrawn, steeped in schmaltz"

indicators.note: something steeped in a liquid sits inside it

parts.note: schmaltz is sickly sentimentality, also called goo
OD is the bank abbreviation for overdrawn

explanation.surface: Someone is relieved to hear a remark described as soaked in sentiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an informal British cry of approval meaning good, glad to hear it.

clue.text: Conventional city?

parts.note: a Swiss city famous for the international treaties on the conduct of war named after it

explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss city gives its name to the treaties on wartime treatment of prisoners, wounded and civilians.

clue.text: Piped music puts only one part of mediocre choir into lead

indicators.note: something mediocre is poor in quality, so the letters are taken as badly arranged

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

explanation.surface: Bagpipe music makes a poor choir sing only one part, slotted under a leading voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts only one part ... into lead' describes the result: I, one letter of the jumbled CHOIR, goes between P and B, giving P(I)B + ROCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A pibroch is a set of variations for the Scottish Highland bagpipe.

clue.text: Question what might produce inflation

definitions.meaning: to question them persistently for information
a bicycle or tyre device that blows air in

explanation.definitionFit: Interrogating someone for facts and a device that inflates tyres share the same word.

clue.text: They're made to scare crew masters

parts.note: a ship's crew are its men
aces are experts or masters at something

explanation.surface: A ship's crew and its expert officers are made to frighten people.
explanation.definitionFit: Threats are made to frighten someone, and the plural noun means threats.

clue.text: One in a train possibly heard to cry feebly

indicators.note: heard means the word is said out loud

parts.note: to mewl is to cry weakly, like a baby or kitten

explanation.surface: A passenger on a train can be heard whimpering.
explanation.walkthrough: Train looks like a railway, but a mule train is a line of pack animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Pack animals travelling in a line form a train, so one of them is a member of it.

clue.text: More than one sea water supply system?

definitions.meaning: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea, so the plural is seas
the pipes carrying public water, gas or electricity to homes

explanation.definitionFit: The poetic plural of the open ocean and the public utility pipe network share one word.

clue.text: The builder, decapitated by Louis VI, pathetically unaware

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: Bob the Builder is a children's TV cartoon character

indicators.note: pathetically suggests something done poorly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A builder is beheaded on the orders of the French king Louis VI, who seems pitifully unaware.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob the Builder is a British children's TV character; 'decapitated' removes his first letter, and 'pathetically' jumbles the French king's name and numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone utterly unaware of what is going on is oblivious to it.
